section_summary: This section closes a Monarch furnace trade-mark inquiry, then documents Standard Oil Development Company’s dispute over registration of its PARAFLOW design in Japan. The larger Parker Pen file concerns allegedly imitated pens and misleading advertising, the search for their manufacturer, and the limits of diplomatic assistance without evidence identifying an infringer.

people.name: Kijuro Ito
people.role: Applicant for the Monarch trade mark in Japan

people.name: H. M. McLarin
people.role: Attorney or trade-mark representative for Standard Oil Development Company

people.name: Y. Iwamura
people.role: Holder of an earlier Japanese design registration

people.name: Katsujiro Nagai
people.role: Japanese applicant for the disputed PARAFLOW design

people.name: Frank A. Howard

people.name: Edgar M. Clark
people.role: Vice president, Standard Oil Development Company

people.role: American chargé d’affaires ad interim in Tokyo

subfiles.title: Monarch case jacket
subfiles.about: Labels the Monarch trade-mark infringement inquiry.
subfiles.summary: Case jacket for the Monarch furnace trade-mark matter.

subfiles.title: Monarch request concerning Japanese trade-mark application
subfiles.about: Requests help opposing Kijuro Ito’s Japanese application for the Monarch mark.
subfiles.summary: The company describes its furnaces and says Ito’s application covers similar goods; the opposition deadline is January 6, 1936.

subfiles.title: State Department reply on Monarch registration
subfiles.from: Green H. Hackworth, Department of State
subfiles.about: Explains the evidence and Japanese legal action needed to oppose Ito’s application.
subfiles.summary: The Department offers an informal embassy inquiry if the company establishes its rights, but advises prompt use of Japan’s formal opposition procedure and local counsel.

subfiles.title: PARAFLOW case jacket
subfiles.about: Labels the PARAFLOW trade-mark file.
subfiles.summary: Case jacket for the PARAFLOW registration dispute.

subfiles.title: McLarin complaint about PARAFLOW registration
subfiles.about: Alleges unfair Japanese treatment of Standard Oil’s PARAFLOW applications.
subfiles.summary: McLarin recounts Standard Oil’s rejected applications, K. Nagai’s later successful appeal for a similar design, and the rejection of a PARAFLOW word-and-design application. He asks for embassy investigation and representations to secure registration.

subfiles.title: Nagai Japanese trade-mark advertisement
subfiles.about: Records publication of Nagai’s application for the disputed design.
subfiles.summary: Advertisement and annotation identify Nagai’s mineral-oil design application and successful appeal.

subfiles.title: Iwamura design registration annotation
subfiles.about: Identifies the earlier registration cited against Standard Oil.
subfiles.summary: Annotated copy identifies Y. Iwamura’s petroleum design registration No. 130818.

subfiles.title: United States PARAFLOW word-and-design registration
subfiles.about: Documents U.S. registration No. 305964 for lubricating oils.
subfiles.summary: Registration used as the basis for Japanese application No. 21752.

subfiles.title: PARAFLOW word-and-design exhibit
subfiles.about: Shows and annotates the mark in Japanese application No. 21752.
subfiles.summary: Design exhibit notes its 1935 filing and 1936 rejection.

subfiles.title: United States PARAFLOW design registration
subfiles.about: Documents U.S. registration No. 312299 for lubricating oils.
subfiles.summary: Registration used as the basis for Japanese application No. 11281.

subfiles.title: PARAFLOW design exhibit
subfiles.about: Identifies the design in Japanese application No. 11281.
subfiles.summary: Caption links the exhibit to the June 1934 Japanese application.

subfiles.title: Department reply to McLarin
subfiles.from: Green H. Hackworth, Department of State
subfiles.about: Agrees to refer the PARAFLOW dispute to Japanese authorities.
subfiles.summary: The Department observes that Standard Oil did not appeal its first rejection, but instructs the embassy to inquire whether the word PARAFLOW can be registered.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Tokyo on PARAFLOW
subfiles.to: Earle R. Dickover, American chargé d’affaires ad interim
subfiles.about: Directs investigation and representations concerning PARAFLOW registration.
subfiles.summary: Enclosing McLarin’s complaint and exhibits, the Department asks the embassy to investigate and urge registration if the facts support the discrimination claim.

subfiles.title: McLarin report of Japanese attorneys’ argument
subfiles.about: Reports the argument filed against rejection of PARAFLOW with design.
subfiles.summary: Quoting Asamura and Higuchi, McLarin argues that the added word distinguishes Standard Oil’s mark from Nagai’s design and recounts Standard Oil’s earlier use and application.

subfiles.title: McLarin report of Japanese attorneys’ argument, duplicate
subfiles.about: Repeats the report of arguments filed for PARAFLOW with design.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of the November 27 report and quoted Japanese legal argument.

subfiles.title: McLarin report of Japanese attorneys’ argument, further duplicate
subfiles.about: Repeats the report of arguments filed for PARAFLOW with design.
subfiles.summary: Further duplicate of the November 27 report.

subfiles.title: McLarin report of Japanese attorneys’ argument, further duplicate
subfiles.about: Repeats the report of arguments filed for PARAFLOW with design.
subfiles.summary: Further duplicate of the November 27 report.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to McLarin
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the Japanese attorneys’ argument.
subfiles.summary: Says a copy will go to the American Embassy in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Forwarding instruction to Ambassador Grew
subfiles.from: Wilbur J. Carr, Department of State
subfiles.about: Forwards McLarin’s account of the Japanese attorneys’ argument.
subfiles.summary: Transmits McLarin’s further letter for the embassy’s PARAFLOW file.

subfiles.title: Embassy despatch on PARAFLOW
subfiles.about: Reports Japan’s reply to embassy representations on PARAFLOW.
subfiles.summary: The embassy confirmed the company’s account and approached the Foreign Office. Grew reports that Japan offers no substantive relief and points the company toward judicial appeal.

subfiles.title: Grew’s note to Foreign Minister Arita
subfiles.about: Urges reversal of Standard Oil’s rejection and approval of PARAFLOW with design.
subfiles.summary: The note describes apparently discriminatory treatment compared with Nagai’s later application.

subfiles.title: Japanese Foreign Minister’s reply and Patent Bureau explanation
subfiles.from: Naotake Satō and Japanese Patent Bureau
subfiles.about: Explains the differing outcomes and available legal appeals.
subfiles.summary: The Patent Bureau says Standard Oil did not appeal its first rejection, while Nagai successfully appealed his. It identifies procedures to challenge Nagai’s registration and Standard Oil’s later rejection.

subfiles.title: Department forwards Japanese reply to McLarin
subfiles.from: Green H. Hackworth, Department of State
subfiles.about: Provides the translated Foreign Office reply.
subfiles.summary: Encloses Japan’s response to the embassy’s PARAFLOW representations.

subfiles.title: McLarin’s response on appeals and nullification
subfiles.about: Reports instructions to appeal and seek nullification of Nagai’s registration.
subfiles.summary: McLarin thanks embassy officers and asks them to continue monitoring the matter.

subfiles.title: Department forwards McLarin update to Grew
subfiles.about: Transmits McLarin’s plans for further Japanese legal action.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the April 28 letter and the Department’s reply.

subfiles.title: Department reply on limits of embassy assistance
subfiles.about: Promises proper assistance while judicial proceedings continue.
subfiles.summary: The embassy may assist but must avoid influencing Japanese judicial authorities.

subfiles.title: McLarin reports Appeal Board rejection
subfiles.about: Reports the rejected PARAFLOW appeal and planned Supreme Court appeal.
subfiles.summary: McLarin says the Appeal Board accepted key facts but applied the law against Standard Oil. He alleges links between Nagai’s registration and a Japanese PARAFLOW importer, and asks the embassy to remain attentive.

subfiles.title: Department reply on prospect of reopening case
subfiles.from: Joseph R. Baker, Department of State
subfiles.about: Responds to the Appeal Board decision and proposed Supreme Court appeal.
subfiles.summary: The Department forwards the materials to Tokyo but doubts a diplomatic basis for reopening the case if Japan’s Supreme Court finally upholds the decision.

subfiles.title: Department forwards Appeal Board papers
subfiles.about: Transmits McLarin’s letter, Appeal Board decision, and Department reply.
subfiles.summary: Forwarding instruction for the embassy’s PARAFLOW file.

subfiles.title: Parker case jacket
subfiles.about: Labels the Parker Pen infringement and advertising complaint.
subfiles.summary: Case jacket for alleged imitation pens and misleading advertising.

subfiles.title: Parker complaint about Saffron pens
subfiles.about: Complains of imitation pens sold as Saffron and falsely associated with Janesville.
subfiles.summary: Parker alleges copying of its instructions and advertising, misuse of its name, and a misleading resemblance to its Safford subsidiary. He asks how to stop sales in the Orient.

subfiles.title: Department reply to Parker
subfiles.from: Green H. Hackworth, Department of State
subfiles.about: Requests patent, trade-mark, and manufacturer details.
subfiles.summary: The Department offers an informal embassy inquiry but explains that infringement generally requires proceedings under Japanese law.

subfiles.title: Tefft supplies Parker registration details
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese registrations and alleged exports of imitation pens.
subfiles.summary: Tefft says VACUMATIC and PARKER are registered in Japan, identifies pending patent applications, and alleges Saffron and other pens are exported from Japan. He cannot identify their manufacturer.

subfiles.title: Parker Vacumatic promotional leaflet
subfiles.about: Advertises Vacumatic pens, visible ink supply, and Quink.
subfiles.summary: Promotional illustrations and claims describe the Vacumatic filling mechanism, capacity, styling, prices, and ink.

subfiles.title: Parker Challenger and Quink leaflet
subfiles.about: Advertises Challenger pens and Quink ink.
subfiles.summary: Leaflet promotes the Deluxe Challenger gift set and Quink’s cleaning claims.

subfiles.title: Parker Vacumatic international price advertisement
subfiles.about: Compares Vacumatic prices in America and Europe.
subfiles.summary: Advertisement promotes ink capacity, visible supply, style, and U.S. price against higher European prices.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Grew on Parker complaint
subfiles.about: Requests an informal inquiry into alleged imitation Parker pens.
subfiles.summary: Encloses Parker correspondence and requests an embassy report.

subfiles.title: Department advises Parker of embassy referral
subfiles.about: Confirms referral of the complaint to the Tokyo embassy.
subfiles.summary: Says the embassy will ask whether Japanese authorities can address the alleged practice.

subfiles.title: Tefft reports rejection of Japanese patent application
subfiles.about: Reports rejection of Parker’s Japanese application for a transparent laminated pen.
subfiles.summary: Tefft says the rejection leaves that feature unprotected in Japan despite a U.S. patent.

subfiles.title: Embassy report on search for imitation Parker pens
subfiles.about: Reports unsuccessful searches for alleged imitation pens or their manufacturer.
subfiles.summary: Commercial and consular officers found no matching pens or identifiable exporter in Japan; the embassy considers an approach to Japanese authorities premature.

subfiles.title: Department reports unsuccessful Parker inquiry
subfiles.from: Green H. Hackworth, Department of State
subfiles.about: Relays the embassy’s unsuccessful investigation.
subfiles.summary: The Department quotes the embassy’s findings and requests stronger evidence before further representations.

subfiles.title: Tefft submits pen advertisement
subfiles.about: Provides an advertisement said to identify a Tokyo imitation-pen manufacturer.
subfiles.summary: Tefft marks a pictured pen as infringing and urges renewed investigation.

subfiles.title: Department requests basis for infringement claim
subfiles.from: Green H. Hackworth, Department of State
subfiles.about: Asks why the pictured pen infringes Parker’s rights.
subfiles.summary: Requests Parker’s reasons to inform any embassy discussion with Japanese authorities.

subfiles.title: Legal Adviser handwritten notes
subfiles.about: Contains fragmentary notes concerning the Parker allegation.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten text is largely illegible in the OCR.

subfiles.title: Consul General’s Parker case despatch
subfiles.about: Submits a proposed reply to Parker for Department review.
subfiles.summary: Garrels notes Parker’s criticism of the handling of its case and requests review of the enclosed consular response.

subfiles.title: Consular reply to Parker, duplicate first page
subfiles.about: Explains legal and evidentiary obstacles to Parker’s claims.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate first page of the consular reply reproduced on pages 235–236.

subfiles.title: Consular reply to Parker
subfiles.about: Explains why identified rights and infringers are needed before action.
subfiles.summary: Garrels says patent priority must be established through legal channels and that unidentified counterfeiters cannot be brought before Japanese authorities on presumption alone.

subfiles.title: Copy of Parker’s original complaint
subfiles.about: Repeats Parker’s complaint about Saffron imitation pens.
subfiles.summary: Copy of the letter on pages 207–208, enclosed in the consular case papers.

subfiles.title: Copy of Department reply to Parker
subfiles.from: Green H. Hackworth, Department of State
subfiles.about: Repeats the Department’s request for rights and manufacturer details.
subfiles.summary: Copy of the reply on pages 209–210.

subfiles.title: Copy of Tefft’s March letter
subfiles.about: Repeats Parker’s registration details and imitation-pen allegations.
subfiles.summary: Copy of the March 18 letter begins here and continues beyond this section.
